name: Anantaraa Golden Triangle Elephant Camp
positioning: Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort: a jungle resort with an elephant camp, on a mountain ridge overlooking the borders of Thailand, Myanmar and Laos
best_for: Travelers who want elephant conservation experiences as part of their stay
Nature lovers who want a bamboo-forest setting with views over three countries
Travelers who want a private tent with its own pool and Golden Triangle views

facts.text: The resort is perched on a mountain ridge overlooking the borders of Thailand, Myanmar and Laos.
The resort is set amid 160 acres of bamboo forest in northern Thailand.
The hotel sits on a sylvan hillside above the Mekong River, an hour north of Chiang Rai.
The resort has an elephant camp with a scientific research and conservation programme.
All accommodations have balconies and teak floors and are decorated with northern Thai objects and textiles.
The Mekong Explorer Suites pay homage to the explorers who charted the Mekong River, blending Lanna traditions with colonial influences.
The infinity pool has Mekong views.
The spa offers spa rituals and ancient healing practices inspired by nature.
A sauna, steam rooms and whirlpool are available, and the tennis court can be booked in advance.
Guests can drift along the Mekong River as morning mist rises, discovering the cultures and landscapes of three neighbouring countries.

highlights.text: Each Mekong Explorer Tent has its own swimming pool and terrace with panoramic views across the Golden Triangle.
From the room balcony, guests can look over three countries and elephants grazing.
The Golden Triangle Asian Elephant Foundation is home to elephants, mahouts and their families, rescued mainly from illegal logging camps, the street or elephant shows.
Guests can journey through the countryside by Royal Enfield sidecar.
At Canopy: Treetop Dining, intimate meals are served high among the branches with views over the surrounding wilderness.

considerations.text: The resort is approximately one hour from Chiang Rai International Airport and a five-minute drive from the historic town of Chiang Saen.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires longer transfers from airports.
